claims.nodeLabel: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection
claims.text: Record Group 615 was established pursuant to sections 1841-1843 of the 2024 National Defense Authorization Act; UAP records received from federal agencies are accessioned into RG 615 and published in the National Archives Catalog on a rolling basis.

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: NARA is custodian without power to compel transmission
edges.note: The Archivist must preserve, index and publish, but Secs. 1842 and 1843 put identification, transmission and postponement in the hands of the agencies and their original classification authorities.

a.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

b.label: Department of War release of UAP files

edges.label: Agency compliance ran nineteen months past the statutory deadline
edges.note: The Sec. 1842(c)(1) agency review deadline fell on 17 October 2024; NARA's transfer guidance is dated April 2025 and the author of the statute described the May 2026 release as the administration only beginning to meet its legal obligation.

a.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

b.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343

edges.label: Collection created by sections 1841-1843 of the FY2024 NDAA
edges.note: The surviving remnant of the Schumer-Rounds UAP Disclosure Act. The 24 April 2025 release drew records from ODNI, OSD, the FAA and the NRC, with rolling additions - the statutory machinery any executive declassification directive must eventually run through.

a.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

b.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)

edges.label: No agency-by-agency compliance accounting is published
edges.note: NARA publishes no list of which agencies have transferred UAP records, no counts and no transfer dates - only a statement that records will be added on a rolling basis as received.

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: Secs. 1841-1843 created RG 615 at the National Archives
edges.note: The collection is the only concrete institution produced by the entire UAPDA fight.

a.label: PURSUE - Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: Two parallel release architectures, only one statutory
edges.note: PURSUE publishes at will through the Secretary's website with no FOIA case numbers or exemption citations, while the statutory NARA collection publishes no compliance accounting - neither channel can be audited.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: FY2024 NDAA, Public Law 118-31 - Div. A, Title XVIII, Subtitle C (secs. 1841-1843), UAP Records Collection; Div. G (IAA FY2024) secs. 7341, 7343

edges.label: Restores the enforcement architecture stripped from the FY2024 sections
edges.note: Sections 1841-1843 created a records collection without a review board, subpoena power or contractor reach; the 2026 amendment reintroduces all three.

a.label: Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Disclosure Act - Burlison amendment to the FY2027 NDAA

b.label: National Archives Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena Records Collection

edges.label: Would impose statutory transfer timelines on the NARA collection
edges.note: The amendment requires agencies to identify, organise, preserve and transmit UAP records to the National Archives on a statutory timeline and creates a Senate-confirmed Records Review Board with subpoena authority.
